chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: The Sunset Club and meeting Prez and Ben Webster
summary: The long narrow Sunset Club on 12th Street where musicians jammed until morning and Prez and Ben Webster befriended him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. So we'd have our little jam sessions in there, and go over to Missouri. We heard old Joe Turner at the Hawaiian Gardens, and we'd go down to the Sunset Club, which was on 12th and Woodland. And that was really something about 10 feet wide, maybe 12 feet wide, maybe 60 feet long.
(chuckle) It was a twit (phonetic) long? sixty feet?

Yeah, and they came on there every night at midnight, but we'd get over there before that. And, you see, I think they hired a piano and a drummer. But sometime there would be maybe 10 musicians up on the stand.
But what--you mean the club was 12 feet long?
About 12 feet wide and about 50 or 60 feet long.
60 feet. Oh, oh, oh.
You know, it was just like goin' down a hallway, like (chuckle), you know.
Oh, I see.
That was Sunset.
A small, narrow place.
Yeah. And that was at Sunset.
I forget what the name of the guy--I know Merle sump'n was the drummer there, one of the musicians. Now this was when
I first met Prez and Ben Webster. And they--
So you're still in college?
Yeah, I'm in college.
Yeah.
They took a liking to me, so they had me coming over there every day, every night, you know, they'd get me --
(End of Side One)
--in the rhythm, you know?
At the Sunset, Gene, there was no room for the bass on the stand, so the rhythm section was just--
Yeah. The rhythm was against the horn players, and they would--
Piano and drums?

Piano and drums there. And they would fight it out 'til daylight, sometime 10 o'clock in the morning. In those days, nobody bothered if you saw a musician, if you heard music at 11:00 o'clock the next morning, you know. Practically all those spook breakfasts went that long. So we'd go over--what's--name--Prez (phonetic) and Ben, they'd come out, and they'd sit and talk to me, you know. They'd say, "Aw, come on--"
